title: Natural Bridge sandstone arch
summary: In Powell and Wolfe counties, Natural Bridge is a 78-foot-long sandstone arch over a gorge of the Red River, carved by uplift, frost, and stream cutting.
bodyMarkdown:
Natural Bridge is a sandstone arch above the Middle Fork of the Red River in eastern Kentucky. It spans 78 feet and stands 65 feet high. Long before it became a railroad attraction and a state park, it was a landmark in country used by Native peoples for thousands of years.

## Stone and time

The [Grokipedia entry on Natural Bridge State Resort Park](https://grokipedia.com/page/Natural_Bridge_State_Resort_Park) says the arch is made of Corbin Sandstone, part of the Breathitt Formation. The rock is more than 90 percent quartz. Rivers laid it down in channels cut into older Mississippian limestones.

That hard sandstone caps softer layers below. Frost wedging, water and differential erosion widened cracks over millions of years until an opening formed beneath the rock. The top of the arch is about 20 feet wide, wide enough for visitors to walk across.

## Native landscape

Grokipedia says the arch was long known to Native peoples and to early settlers as a landmark. The surrounding Red River Gorge holds many rockshelters with evidence of Native life, including early plant cultivation at sites such as [Newt Kash](/stories/newt-kash-hollow-15mf1/) and [Cloudsplitter](/stories/cloudsplitter-rockshelter-menifee-county/), as described in the [Grokipedia entry on the Red River Gorge](https://grokipedia.com/page/Red_River_Gorge).

## A railroad attraction

Railroads brought tourists. The [Wikipedia article on the park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_Bridge_State_Resort_Park) says the Lexington and Eastern Railroad opened the site as a private tourist attraction in 1895. Grokipedia says Kentucky Union Railway executives began building toward the area in 1889, partly to reach timber. Excursion trains then carried visitors from cities such as Cincinnati.

The park's half-mile "Original Trail" to the arch dates from the 1890s. In 1910 the Louisville and Nashville Railroad bought the Lexington and Eastern and with it the Natural Bridge land.

## A state park

In 1926 L&N president Wible L. Mapother turned over about 137 acres to the new Kentucky State Park Commission. That made Natural Bridge one of Kentucky's four original state parks. Grokipedia says Hemlock Lodge opened in 1927 and 940 acres were added in 1929.

## Kentucky today

Natural Bridge State Resort Park, in Powell and Wolfe counties, borders the Daniel Boone National Forest and the [Red River Gorge](/stories/red-river-gorge-arches-and-the-dam-fight/). Visitors can hike to the arch or ride a skylift, seasonally, to the top. Part of the park is a state nature preserve, and the Sheltowee Trace trail runs through it.
